findings.title: Main description is too pale for my eyes
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: I cannot comfortably read this low-contrast, fine text, and the unfamiliar words make the service sound confusing rather than warm and trustworthy.

findings.title: The main introductory language is needlessly technical
findings.evidence: “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus”
findings.why: I have to stop and work out what those phrases mean before I know what the website will do.

findings.title: The main image has no description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 577x440]
findings.why: A screen reader will not tell me what the illustration shows, and at this zoom I can see only part of it.

findings.title: Footer links and copyright text are too faint and small
findings.evidence: “Privacy”; “Terms”; “Contact”; “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.”
findings.why: I cannot make these out, so important information about privacy, terms, and who runs the service is inaccessible to me.

findings.title: The primary call to action does not say what happens next
findings.evidence: [5] link “Proceed →”
findings.why: “Proceed” could lead to signing up, paying, or entering family details. I would hesitate before clicking a control with unclear consequences.

findings.title: Email and password fields have placeholders but no permanent labels
findings.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder “Email”; [6] textbox (no label) placeholder “Password”
findings.why: The words are clear now, but a visible label is steadier than a placeholder, especially when fields already contain information or a screen reader is used.

findings.title: Footer information is too faint and small to read
findings.evidence: The links to Privacy, Terms, Contact, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are described as faint and small.
findings.why: I cannot make out these words at 200% zoom, so I cannot check the privacy, terms, or contact information.

findings.title: Unexplained technical error after login
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: It sounds as though part of my account has failed, so I may be worried that my details or the book will be lost.

findings.title: Error code is technical and unexplained
findings.why: A hexadecimal code is not useful to me and makes an ordinary account problem seem more serious than it may be.

findings.title: Faint secondary text
findings.evidence: “You have no books yet.” is pale grey
findings.why: At 200% zoom I can just about see it, but the low contrast makes the page harder to read.

findings.title: Footer text is too faint to read
findings.evidence: The footer links [7], [8], and [9] are described as faint/small and I cannot make them out.
findings.why: I cannot find the privacy, terms, or contact information, which I may need before trusting the service with family memories.

findings.title: Important form fields are hidden below the fold at high zoom
findings.evidence: “What do they look like? (optional),” “Who else is in the story?,” and the “Next” button are all marked “offscreen.”
findings.why: At 200% zoom I can easily miss fields or the Next button, so I need to scroll through slowly and check what I have missed.

findings.title: Footer text is too faint to read
findings.evidence: The Privacy, Terms, Contact, and copyright text is described as faint and unreadable.
findings.why: Pale grey writing is effectively invisible to me, so I cannot check the terms, privacy information, or contact details here.

findings.title: Back does not explain whether the later story answers were kept
findings.evidence: After clicking “Back” on the story-details page, the site returned to “Who's the star of the story?” without any message about the entered story details.
findings.why: I may lose the long description of Conker without realising it, then have to type the whole thing again.

findings.title: Placeholder text is too faint
findings.evidence: The examples “e.g. the beach at Grandma's”, “e.g. a yellow bucket”, and “What happened? Why does it matter to your family?” are pale grey inside the boxes.
findings.why: At 200% zoom I can just make out the examples, but the paler writing takes extra effort and is not a reliable guide.

findings.title: No visible confirmation that character details were saved
findings.evidence: After the previous Next action, the page changed directly to “Your story” without a message saying Lily’s details were saved.
findings.why: The change does show progress, but a brief confirmation would reassure me that I have not lost the information I entered.

findings.title: The memory box silently keeps only 200 characters
findings.evidence: Textbox [18] shows 200 characters ending with “carved Conker from wood in his workshop shed, wor…”.
findings.why: The omitted ending includes the important moment when I gave Conker to Lily and her ride across the fields, so the book may not contain the memory I intended.

findings.title: Reading levels are labelled in specialist terms
findings.evidence: The choices are “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L” and “Lexile 800L+”.
findings.why: I have to guess which range suits Lily, and getting it wrong would mean making a book that is too advanced for her.

findings.title: Footer text is too faint to read
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms” and “Contact” are described as faint small text that I cannot make out.
findings.why: I cannot check the privacy, terms or contact details when the letters are this pale.

findings.title: Photo upload lacks a proper visible field label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label); the screen only shows the native control “Choose file” and “No file chosen”.
findings.why: The small native control is harder to see and understand at 200% zoom, and I cannot tell from the control itself that it is specifically for Lily's face.

findings.title: Footer text is faint and too small to read
findings.evidence: [13] link [faint/small text you cannot make out]; [14] link [faint/small text you cannot make out]; [15] link [faint/small text you cannot make out]
findings.why: I cannot read or confidently use the privacy, terms, or contact links.

findings.title: The title contains a spelling mistake
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Lily”
findings.why: This is meant to be a keepsake for Lily, and seeing a spelling error on the cover makes the whole present feel less finished.

findings.title: Chosen illustration style was not followed
findings.evidence: I selected “Watercolour — soft and dreamy,” but the preview says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.”
findings.why: I deliberately chose a style, and this change was not explained; it makes me wonder what else from my choices was ignored.

findings.title: Page controls are small and symbol-only
findings.evidence: [6] button "‹" and [7] button "›"; the controls are described as tiny and hard to hit at 200% zoom.
findings.why: I need to check every page, but small arrow buttons are awkward to hit and I cannot be certain what they mean.

findings.title: Paid regeneration is prominent without explaining the effect
findings.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
findings.why: I am cautious about costs, and it is not clear whether this would replace my current book and whether anything could be restored afterwards.

findings.title: Page content appears below the cover image rather than as a clear page-reading area
findings.evidence: The page lists “The Magical Adventrue of Lily,” “A StoryHearth original,” and the style after the cover image.
findings.why: It is not immediately clear whether these lines are part of the book or preview metadata.

findings.title: Footer text has insufficient visibility
findings.evidence: The “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” links are described as faint and too small to read.
findings.why: Pale writing is effectively invisible to me, so these ordinary links are not usable.

findings.title: Page navigation buttons are very small
findings.evidence: [6] and [7] are tiny arrow buttons, with [7] labelled only “›”
findings.why: At 200% zoom I have trouble hitting small controls, and an arrow-only label does not tell me what it will do.

findings.title: Generated book title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Lily”
findings.why: This is meant to be a keepsake book for Lily, so a misspelled title makes it look careless.

findings.title: The final sentence is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Lily looked up at the sky, she would always remember”
findings.why: The book ends without telling me what Lily remembers, so it does not feel finished or good enough to give to her.

findings.title: Gift wrap is selected without being requested
findings.evidence: Control [6] says “Premium gift wrap” and is checked; it adds “£7.99” to the £45.97 total.
findings.why: I might mistakenly pay for something I did not want, and I do not trust a bill that starts with an extra already selected.

findings.title: The core delivery cost is not summarised clearly
findings.evidence: The page shows “Hardcover” £24.99 and “Shipping & handling” £12.99, but the prominently displayed “Total” is £45.97 because of the selected extra.
findings.why: I need to know the straightforward price of the hardcover arriving at my door, without doing sums and hunting for what caused it.

findings.title: Checkout timer creates needless pressure
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57” is shown in prominent red text.
findings.why: I read carefully and may not finish checking in ten minutes; a countdown makes me rush or worry that I have missed the book.

findings.title: Legal and contact links are unreadable
findings.evidence: Links [12], [13], and [14] are marked “faint/small text you cannot make out”; the footer also includes unreadable text.
findings.why: I cannot check the privacy, terms, or contact details before deciding whether to trust the company, even at 200% zoom.

findings.title: The price-reservation timer may create unnecessary urgency
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:35”
findings.why: A countdown can make me feel hurried, even though I only wanted to check the cost.

findings.title: There is no clear way to leave checkout without losing my place
findings.evidence: The visible checkout controls are “Premium gift wrap,” the address and payment fields, and the links at the bottom; no “Cancel,” “Back,” or “Save and finish later” control is visible.
findings.why: I want to inspect the price and stop without risking an accidental order or losing my book.
